entries.sourceText: - **451. Short-term vs long-term** \[Slider\]: a clickbait change wins this week and loses users over months; surrogate metrics try to predict that.
entries.title: Immediate clicks versus later value
entries.lens: the horizon-specific incremental value assumption

entries.sourceText: - **452. Bank run** \[Slider\]: set how many depositors fear a run and watch it become self-fulfilling.
entries.title: A fear-driven toy withdrawal loop
entries.lens: the amplification rule in a stipulated bank-run model

entries.sourceText: - **453. Lucas critique** \[Gotcha\]: relationships in past data change once people react to a new policy.
entries.title: A policy changes the fitted response
entries.lens: the assumed coefficient after people react to a policy

entries.sourceText: - **454. Braess's paradox** \[Gotcha\]: adding a road to a network can make everyone's commute slower.
entries.title: A shortcut can raise equilibrium time
entries.lens: selfish routing on the specified symmetric network

entries.sourceText: - **455. Seasonal confounding** \[Slider\]: a campaign launched in December looks great because of Christmas.
entries.title: A holiday changes both groups
entries.lens: the seasonal comparison removed by a control trend

entries.sourceText: - **456. Autocorrelation** \[Gotcha\]: treating correlated days as independent makes noise look highly significant.
entries.title: Correlated days reduce effective draws
entries.lens: the mean-variance ESS of a specified AR(1) series

entries.sourceText: - **457. The drunk and her dog** \[Slider\]: two random walks that wander but stay tied together, cointegration in one picture.
entries.title: Two wandering levels share a gap
entries.lens: the common trend removed by differencing

entries.sourceText: - **458. Time-varying confounding** \[Gotcha\]: today's treatment changes tomorrow's health, which guides tomorrow's treatment.
entries.title: Treatment changes a later mediator
entries.lens: the mediated path in a two-stage structural toy model

entries.sourceText: - **459. Anticipation** \[Gotcha\]: people change behavior before a policy starts, contaminating the "before" period.
entries.title: Anticipation contaminates the before
entries.lens: the chosen pretreatment baseline in a contrast

entries.sourceText: - **460. MusicLab** \[Story\]: in parallel worlds of the same song market, early download counts drove wildly different hits (Salganik, Dodds & Watts, 2006).
entries.title: An early lead gets amplified
entries.lens: the initial condition in a stipulated popularity recurrence

entries.sourceText: - **461. PC algorithm, step by step** \[Slider\]: start fully connected, delete edges with independence tests, then orient colliders.
entries.title: One conditional-independence step
entries.lens: the isolated path test used as a discovery ingredient

entries.sourceText: - **462. Which way is the arrow?** \[Predict\]: see a scatter and guess cause vs effect; noise that's even around the curve in one direction reveals it.
entries.title: A direction must be stipulated here
entries.lens: a structural direction rather than direction inferred from scatter

entries.sourceText: - **463. Non-Gaussian clue** \[Slider\]: with non-normal noise, a linear model's direction becomes identifiable (LiNGAM).
entries.title: A non-Gaussian noise clue
entries.lens: the asymmetry of a specified noise distribution

entries.sourceText: - **464. Cause–effect pairs** \[Measure\]: guess directions for real pairs like altitude and temperature; score yourself against algorithms.
entries.title: A proposed direction needs a model
entries.lens: observation versus intervention with a declared direction

entries.sourceText: - **465. Poke the system** \[Slider\]: intervene on one variable at a time and watch the arrows lock into place.
entries.title: Poke the variable rather than observe
entries.lens: the incoming common-cause edge removed by an intervention

entries.sourceText: - **466. Double machine learning** \[Slider\]: residualize treatment and outcome with ML, then regress residual on residual.
entries.title: Regress residual on residual
entries.lens: the residual projection ingredient of a causal estimator

entries.sourceText: - **467. Naive ML bias** \[Gotcha\]: plugging a regularized ML model straight into a causal estimate biases it.
entries.title: Regularization can shrink a slope
entries.lens: the coefficient bias of a stipulated ridge fit

entries.sourceText: - **468. Hidden confounder** \[Gotcha\]: discovery algorithms draw confident arrows that a missing variable fully explains.
entries.title: A missing common cause explains a link
entries.lens: the unobserved common-cause path in a toy graph

entries.sourceText: - **469. Cancelling paths** \[Gotcha\]: a drug's direct and indirect effects cancel, so the data shows no dependence at all.
entries.title: Direct and indirect paths cancel
entries.lens: the total derivative when two structural paths oppose

entries.sourceText: - **470. Invariance across environments** \[Slider\]: the true causes predict equally well in every hospital; spurious features don't.
entries.title: A structural slope across contexts
entries.lens: the invariant direct term versus context-dependent association

entries.sourceText: - **471. Cows on beaches** \[Gotcha\]: a classifier fails on cows outside grassy fields because it learned the background.
entries.title: A background shortcut meets a new mix
entries.lens: the group composition behind a toy classifier accuracy

entries.sourceText: - **472. The hospital tag** \[Story\]: a pneumonia model picked up which hospital took the X-ray rather than the lungs (Zech et al., 2018).
entries.title: A hospital shortcut depends on mix
entries.lens: the population mix of a stipulated shortcut classifier

entries.sourceText: - **473. Domain shift** \[Slider\]: shift patient mix between hospitals and watch a predictive model's accuracy collapse.
entries.title: Shift the population, keep group scores
entries.lens: composition change with fixed group-level performance

entries.sourceText: - **474. Counterfactual augmentation** \[Slider\]: flip a review's sentiment words but not its topic, and retrain to cut shortcuts.
entries.title: Change a stipulated sentiment feature
entries.lens: a fixed structural decoder rather than a retrained model

entries.sourceText: - **475. Disentangling factors** \[Slider\]: slide one latent dimension at a time and watch a generated face change only in pose or light.
entries.title: Two separately controlled toy factors
entries.lens: the decoder's constructed separation of angle and light

entries.sourceText: - **476. Ask a chatbot** \[Split\]: pose correlational and interventional versions of the same question and compare its answers.
entries.title: Seeing and doing ask different things
entries.lens: the declared structural model behind two differently worded queries

entries.sourceText: - **477. Diagnosis network** \[Slider\]: toggle symptoms and test results; posterior probabilities of diseases update.
entries.title: A symptom updates a supplied prior
entries.lens: one diagnostic-network update with stated likelihoods

entries.sourceText: - **478. Root cause in microservices** \[Slider\]: a latency spike spreads across services; trace it back along the causal graph.
entries.title: A latency change travels along a path
entries.lens: the direct and propagated terms of a toy service dependency

entries.sourceText: - **479. Robust under intervention** \[Split\]: a causal and a predictive model face a policy change; only one keeps working.
entries.title: A predictive slope under intervention
entries.lens: the structural derivative after changing assignment

entries.sourceText: - **480. Greedy score search** \[Slider\]: add, remove and flip arrows to improve a graph's fit score, step by step.
entries.title: Score a candidate graph
entries.lens: likelihood gain versus a parameter-count penalty

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **481. The Broad Street pump** \[Story\]: John Snow mapped 1854 cholera deaths around one London water pump.
entries.title: A pump comparison needs denominators
entries.lens: the descriptive rate contrast in an illustrative exposure table

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **482. Smoking and lung cancer** \[Story\]: Doll and Hill's 1950 study and their later British doctors cohort tied smoking to lung cancer.
entries.title: An association and its common cause
entries.lens: the observation-intervention gap in a stipulated risk-score model

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **483. Fisher's objection** \[Story\]: Fisher argued a gene might cause both smoking and cancer; Cornfield showed such a confounder would need implausible strength (1959).
entries.title: How strong is a stipulated sensitivity?
entries.lens: the specified risk-ratio sensitivity function

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **484. Hormone therapy reversal** \[Story\]: observational studies suggested heart protection; the 2002 Women's Health Initiative trial found harm.
entries.title: A healthy-user story can reverse a sign
entries.lens: confounding that opposes a stipulated intervention effect

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **485. Beta-carotene** \[Story\]: a 1994 Finnish trial found beta-carotene supplements *raised* lung cancer in smokers.
entries.title: A treatment can increase toy risk
entries.lens: the sign of an explicit absolute risk change

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **486. Semmelweis** \[Story\]: in 1847, handwashing with chlorinated lime cut deaths in his maternity clinic dramatically.
entries.title: A clinic before-after rate contrast
entries.lens: the denominator in an illustrative infection-count comparison

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **487. The Lanarkshire milk experiment** \[Story\]: teachers swapped frailer kids into the milk group, ruining a 1930 trial of 20,000 children (Student, 1931).
entries.title: Frail children select into treatment
entries.lens: baseline severity in a nonrandom treatment assignment

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **488. Tennessee STAR** \[Story\]: students randomly assigned to smaller classes in 1985–89 did better on tests.
entries.title: A stipulated small-class effect
entries.lens: the difference between two modeled educational outcomes

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **489. Sally Clark** \[Story\]: a "1 in 73 million" figure squared a single-death probability, assuming independence; her conviction was overturned in 2003.
entries.title: Squaring requires an assumption
entries.lens: the conditional probability needed for a joint rare event

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **490. Challenger** \[Story\]: plotting O-ring damage only for flights *with* damage hid the link to cold launch temperatures.
entries.title: Leaving out the undamaged cases
entries.lens: outcome-dependent selection in a damage sample

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **491. Google Flu Trends** \[Story\]: search-based flu estimates overshot the 2012–13 season by roughly double.
entries.title: A probability forecast can overshoot
entries.lens: the gap between a stated forecast and observed frequency

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **492. Dewey Defeats Truman** \[Story\]: quota-sampled polls in 1948 got the US election wrong.
entries.title: A quota sample has a composition
entries.lens: the group weights behind a toy electoral estimate

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **493. Moving to Opportunity** \[Story\]: children whose families won housing vouchers when young earned more as adults (Chetty, Hendren & Katz, 2016).
entries.title: Age groups can have different effects
entries.lens: the target population behind a heterogeneous intervention

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **494. The polio vaccine trial** \[Story\]: the 1954 Salk field trial involved about 1.8 million children, with a randomized placebo arm.
entries.title: A randomized comparison still has counts
entries.lens: the descriptive risk difference in a toy trial table

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **495. Scurvy** \[Story\]: in 1747 James Lind compared six treatments on sailors; citrus worked.
entries.title: Compare two stipulated remedy groups
entries.lens: the denominators of an illustrative treatment comparison

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **496. Hawthorne revisited** \[Story\]: reanalysis of the original factory lighting data found little support for the famous effect (Levitt & List, 2011).
entries.title: A famous story meets later evidence
entries.lens: the sensitivity to which study estimates are included

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **497. Streptomycin** \[Story\]: the 1948 UK Medical Research Council trial was among the first properly randomized clinical trials.
entries.title: A trial contrast in standardized units
entries.lens: the outcome spread behind a standardized estimate

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **498. The Netflix Prize** \[Story\]: teams blended hundreds of models to beat Netflix's recommender by 10%, winning $1 million in 2009.
entries.title: A blended predictor under toy risks
entries.lens: the stipulated variance reduction in an ensemble risk calculation

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **499. Observing Dark Worlds** \[Story\]: a 2012 Kaggle contest asked teams to locate invisible dark matter halos from distorted galaxy shapes; Bayesian MCMC models took the top two places.
entries.title: One-axis halo-location update
entries.lens: a normal measurement ingredient rather than full shear inference

entries.sourceSection: 25. Famous real-world causal and probability stories
entries.sourceText: - **500. A 29% chance happens** \[Story\]: forecasts giving Trump about a 29% chance in 2016 weren't "wrong" when he won; one-in-three events are common.
entries.title: One outcome does not judge a forecast
entries.lens: repeated calibration versus a single realized election

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **502. The hockey stick** \[Slider\]: plot average wait against utilization; going from 80% to 90% busy doubles the wait.
entries.title: Near capacity, waiting grows sharply
entries.lens: the load gap in a stable queueing model

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **504. Random vs fixed service** \[Split\]: same average service time; fixed times cut queue waits in half (M/M/1 vs M/D/1).
entries.title: Fixed service removes one variance term
entries.lens: service variability with the same average service time

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **505. Variability kills** \[Slider\]: keep the average service time, raise its variance, and watch the queue grow.
entries.title: The same service mean, different tails
entries.lens: the second moment of service in an M/G/1 mean wait

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **506. Add a second barista** \[Predict\]: waits fall by far more than half, often by over 90% at high load.
entries.title: Add another pooled server
entries.lens: the pooled-server waiting probability and delay

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **507. One fast or two slow?** \[Split\]: one server at double speed vs two normal servers; compare waits and total time.
entries.title: One fast server or two slower ones
entries.lens: waiting and total time at equal total service capacity

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **508. Merge the call centers** \[Slider\]: pool ten small centers into one and see the same service level with fewer agents.
entries.title: Pooling removes isolated spare capacity
entries.lens: the symmetric single-center versus pooled-center model

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **509. Bursty arrivals** \[Slider\]: same average arrival rate, but in bursts; the queue looks completely different.
entries.title: Bursts raise the variability factor
entries.lens: arrival variability in a stated queueing approximation

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **510. Balking and reneging** \[Slider\]: customers who see a long line leave, or give up after waiting; watch lost sales.
entries.title: Some queued customers abandon the sale
entries.lens: the retained-customer share in a supplied service funnel

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **511. Erlang C staffing** \[Slider\]: how many agents are needed to answer 80% of calls within 20 seconds?
entries.title: A service threshold enters Erlang C
entries.lens: the staffing input of an explicit queueing model

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **512. Square-root staffing** \[Slider\]: as call volume grows, the safety margin of extra agents grows only with its square root.
entries.title: The reserve scales with a square root
entries.lens: the stated staffing-rule safety margin

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **513. Warm-up period** \[Predict\]: an empty queue takes time to reach steady state; early measurements mislead.
entries.title: A snapshot depends on its starting queue
entries.lens: the transient starting state of a deterministic fluid queue

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **514. PASTA** \[Gotcha\]: random arrivals see the average queue; scheduled arrivals, like booked appointments, don't.
entries.title: Long states get more time exposure
entries.lens: time-weighted observation rather than a general PASTA proof

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **515. Restaurant tables** \[Slider\]: tune reservations vs walk-ins and see table turnover and waits.
entries.title: A toy pooled-table capacity model
entries.lens: steady Poisson arrivals rather than a reservation schedule

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **516. Skyscraper elevators** \[Slider\]: morning rush in a 40-floor building; zoning floors to elevators cuts waits.
entries.title: Stops add overhead to an elevator round
entries.lens: the deterministic timing facet of floor zoning

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **517. Virtual queue** \[Split\]: a theme-park ride with and without return-time tickets; same capacity, very different experience.
entries.title: A virtual place moves the waiting
entries.lens: in-line time without changing the stipulated total wait

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **518. Express lane threshold** \[Slider\]: set the item limit and watch both lanes' waits balance.
entries.title: A shorter-job lane changes service mix
entries.lens: the service distribution supplied to a toy express queue

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **519. ER at 95% capacity** \[Slider\]: push a hospital emergency department near full and watch boarding delays cascade.
entries.title: Little slack near full capacity
entries.lens: the nonlinear waiting-time effect near service capacity

entries.sourceSection: 26. Queueing theory: single queues & Little's law
entries.sourceText: - **520. Kingman's formula** \[Slider\]: wait ≈ variability × utilization × service time, with each factor on its own slider.
entries.title: Variability, load and service duration
entries.lens: the three factors in a stated heavy-traffic approximation

entries.sourceText: - **522. Shortest queue vs random** \[Split\]: watch two server farms side by side, one routing randomly, one to the shortest line.
entries.title: One arrival can choose the shorter line
entries.lens: routing with observed equal-duration jobs

entries.sourceText: - **523. Load balancer showdown** \[Slider\]: round robin vs least-connections under uneven job sizes.
entries.title: Few jobs can mean much outstanding work
entries.lens: job counts versus remaining workload

entries.sourceText: - **525. FIFO, LIFO, sharing** \[Split\]: the same jobs under three scheduling rules; compare waits and fairness.
entries.title: Which of two jobs goes first?
entries.lens: the mean wait in two explicitly ordered jobs

entries.sourceText: - **526. The tail at scale** \[Gotcha\]: fan a request out to 100 servers and one server's rare slowness becomes the typical user's experience (Dean & Barroso, 2013).
entries.title: A fan-out inherits one slow component
entries.lens: the union of independent slow-request events

entries.sourceText: - **527. Hedged requests** \[Slider\]: send a backup request after a short delay and cut tail latency for a little extra load.
entries.title: Independent backups must both be slow
entries.lens: the joint slow-tail event in a two-copy toy model

entries.sourceText: - **528. Factory network** \[Slider\]: jobs flow through linked stations; the busiest one sets everyone's pace.
entries.title: A serial line has one limiting station
entries.lens: the smallest supplied station capacity

entries.sourceText: - **529. Find the bottleneck** \[Predict\]: guess which station limits a production line, then speed it up and watch the bottleneck move.
entries.title: Speed up the binding station
entries.lens: the movement of a deterministic capacity bottleneck

entries.sourceText: - **530. WIP limits** \[Slider\]: cap work in progress on a kanban board and watch cycle time fall.
entries.title: Less work at the same throughput
entries.lens: compatible long-run WIP and throughput averages

entries.sourceText: - **531. Retry storms** \[Slider\]: a brief slowdown triggers retries that keep the system overloaded long after the cause is gone.
entries.title: Retries can exceed available capacity
entries.lens: the stipulated effective arrival rate after retries

entries.sourceText: - **532. Backpressure** \[Slider\]: let a slow service push back on callers and the pile-up stops spreading.
entries.title: Backpressure caps the incoming rate
entries.lens: the fluid input-capacity gap

entries.sourceText: - **533. Autoscaling lag** \[Slider\]: new servers take minutes to start; a traffic spike outruns them.
entries.title: Scaling lag gives a deficit time to grow
entries.lens: the duration of a stipulated capacity shortfall

entries.sourceText: - **534. Head-of-line blocking** \[Gotcha\]: one slow job at the front stalls fast jobs behind it.
entries.title: The long front job delays a short job
entries.lens: the two-job head-of-line waiting calculation

entries.sourceText: - **535. Priority starvation** \[Slider\]: raise high-priority traffic and watch low-priority jobs never get served.
entries.title: High priority consumes the spare service
entries.lens: the residual capacity available to a low-priority fluid queue

entries.sourceText: - **536. Traffic light timing** \[Slider\]: tune green times at an intersection and see queues on each road.
entries.title: A green-time share sets average capacity
entries.lens: the supplied signal duty cycle in a fluid model

entries.sourceText: - **537. Airport security** \[Slider\]: open or close lanes as flights bunch up and see missed-flight risk.
entries.title: An extra security lane changes the wait
entries.lens: the server count in a stated steady queue

entries.sourceText: - **538. Ride-hailing dispatch** \[Slider\]: drivers cycle between idle, en route and busy; demand spikes drain idle drivers.
entries.title: Idle drivers are an inflow-outflow stock
entries.lens: the assumed returns and request rates of an idle-driver buffer

entries.sourceText: - **539. The bus loop** \[Slider\]: one server visiting several queues in turn; buses bunch together over time.
entries.title: A fixed polling loop pays switch time
entries.lens: the one-job-per-visit timing facet of a polling cycle

entries.sourceText: - **540. Your team's queue** \[Measure\]: enter work in progress and throughput to compute your team's average cycle time with Little's law.
entries.title: Turn team WIP into a cycle-time estimate
entries.lens: the long-run system boundary required by Little's law

entries.sourceText: - **542. Split and merge streams** \[Slider\]: thin one Poisson stream into two, or merge two into one; both stay Poisson.
entries.title: Thin, then merge independent streams
entries.lens: independent thinning and superposition rates

entries.sourceText: - **543. Traffic by hour** \[Slider\]: draw a daily arrival-rate curve and watch visits pulse with it.
entries.title: Integrate a changing hourly arrival rate
entries.lens: the area under a stated linear intensity

entries.sourceText: - **544. Aftershocks** \[Slider\]: a self-exciting Hawkes process where each event raises the chance of more, like earthquakes or retweets.
entries.title: Events create expected descendants
entries.lens: the subcritical offspring multiplier

entries.sourceText: - **545. Replacing bulbs** \[Slider\]: a renewal process; tune lifetime spread and see replacement timing smooth out.
entries.title: Renewal spread changes the residual wait
entries.lens: the second-moment inspection effect at a fixed mean lifetime

entries.sourceText: - **546. Insurance claims** \[Slider\]: random claim times with random sizes; total payout builds in jumps.
entries.title: A random count of random claims
entries.lens: claim-count and claim-size uncertainty

entries.sourceText: - **548. Extinction threshold** \[Slider\]: average offspring below 1 always dies out; just above 1 often still dies.
entries.title: Subcritical and supercritical lineages
entries.lens: the eventual extinction fixed point

entries.sourceText: - **549. Family tree** \[Predict\]: grow a random branching tree and guess whether it survives 20 generations.
entries.title: Extinction by a finite generation
entries.lens: the generating-function iterate before the eventual limit

entries.sourceText: - **550. Mean reversion** \[Slider\]: an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck path wanders but keeps being pulled back to its mean.
entries.title: An expected path returns toward its mean
entries.lens: conditional mean reversion in a stipulated diffusion

entries.sourceText: - **551. Stock price paths** \[Slider\]: geometric Brownian motion; raise volatility and the fan of paths widens.
entries.title: Volatility separates mean and median
entries.lens: the lognormal terminal distribution under specified parameters

entries.sourceText: - **552. Lévy flight vs random walk** \[Split\]: a few huge jumps vs many small steps, the two styles of animal foraging.
entries.title: Rare long jumps change a bounded mean
entries.lens: a finite jump-mixture facet rather than a stable Levy process

entries.sourceText: - **553. Random telegraph** \[Slider\]: a signal that flips between two states at random times.
entries.title: A two-state signal forgets its start
entries.lens: continuous-time transition rates in a two-state signal

entries.sourceText: - **554. Immigration and death** \[Slider\]: a population fed by arrivals and drained by deaths settles into a Poisson-shaped balance.
entries.title: Arrivals offset per-capita departures
entries.lens: the mean balance of an immigration-death model

entries.sourceText: - **555. Genetic drift** \[Slider\]: in a Moran model, a neutral gene randomly takes over or vanishes in a small population.
entries.title: A neutral allele can take over
entries.lens: the initial frequency under a neutral finite-population model

entries.sourceText: - **556. Wright–Fisher** \[Slider\]: watch many allele-frequency paths drift to 0 or 1, faster in small populations.
entries.title: Small populations drift more
entries.lens: the conditional one-generation Wright-Fisher spread

entries.sourceText: - **557. Clustered, random or regular?** \[Split\]: three tree maps; guess which is Poisson, which clustered, which repulsive.
entries.title: Uniform placement still leaves gaps
entries.lens: the empty-cell baseline of an independent spatial toy model

entries.sourceText: - **558. Voronoi cells** \[Slider\]: drop random seed points and the plane splits into cells, like cracked mud or giraffe spots.
entries.title: The boundary between two line seeds
entries.lens: the one-dimensional equal-distance Voronoi boundary

entries.sourceText: - **559. First passage** \[Slider\]: how long until a Brownian path first hits a barrier? The distribution has a heavy tail.
entries.title: First hit within a finite horizon
entries.lens: the absorbing finite-lattice analogue of first passage

entries.sourceText: - **560. Brownian bridge** \[Slider\]: random paths pinned at both ends, the shape behind many statistical tests.
entries.title: Pin both ends of a random path
entries.lens: the Brownian-bridge variance profile

entries.sourceText: - **563. How fast does it mix?** \[Slider\]: plot distance from uniform after each shuffle of a deck.
entries.title: A chain approaches stationarity
entries.lens: the exact two-state total-variation distance

entries.sourceText: - **564. The cutoff** \[Gotcha\]: some chains stay far from mixed, then mix almost all at once.
entries.title: A collection transition can be sharp
entries.lens: the coupon-completion analogy rather than a general cutoff theorem

entries.sourceText: - **565. Absorbing states** \[Predict\]: guess the expected steps until a board game ends, then compute it exactly.
entries.title: Absorption time in a finite toy board
entries.lens: the expected stopping time between two absorbing boundaries

entries.sourceText: - **566. Hitting probabilities** \[Slider\]: from each square, the chance of reaching the goal before the trap, colored live.
entries.title: The goal competes with a trap
entries.lens: the fair-walk hitting probability between two boundaries

entries.sourceText: - **567. Detailed balance** \[Slider\]: flows between each pair of states cancel, a property that MCMC relies on.
entries.title: Forward and reverse stationary flow
entries.lens: detailed balance in a specified two-state chain

entries.sourceText: - **568. Periodic chains** \[Gotcha\]: a chain that alternates between two sets never settles, even though it has a stationary distribution.
entries.title: A periodic chain keeps its oscillation
entries.lens: a stationary law without convergence from a fixed start

entries.sourceText: - **569. Spectral gap** \[Slider\]: the second eigenvalue sets the mixing speed; drag graph edges and watch it change.
entries.title: The second eigenvalue changes the decay
entries.lens: the spectral-gap facet of a two-state mixing model

entries.sourceText: - **570. Barbell graph** \[Slider\]: two dense clusters joined by one edge mix very slowly.
entries.title: A tiny cross-cluster transition is slow
entries.lens: the coarse two-state bottleneck analogy

entries.sourceText: - **571. Customer journeys** \[Slider\]: model site pages as states and watch visitors flow to purchase or exit.
entries.title: A toy journey reaches a purchase stage
entries.lens: the conditional probabilities in a finite conversion path

entries.sourceText: - **572. Removal effect attribution** \[Slider\]: delete one channel from the journey chain and see how many conversions vanish.
entries.title: A modeled channel-removal contrast
entries.lens: the specified without-channel counterfactual

entries.sourceText: - **573. Credit ratings** \[Slider\]: yearly transitions between AAA and default; project a bond's path decades out.
entries.title: A constant annual default hazard
entries.lens: the survival complement under a constant conditional hazard

entries.sourceText: - **574. Markov melodies** \[Slider\]: generate music from note-transition probabilities, then raise the order.
entries.title: A two-note Markov melody
entries.lens: the next-state mixture in a stipulated note-transition model

entries.sourceText: - **575. Coupling from the past** \[Slider\]: run chains from every start until they merge, giving an exact sample.
entries.title: Independent chances for a coupling event
entries.lens: a supplied coalescence-opportunity model rather than full CFTP

entries.sourceText: - **576. Ising magnet** \[Slider\]: flip spins on a grid at a set temperature; below a critical point, big domains form.
entries.title: One spin listens to its neighbors
entries.lens: the conditional probability at one Ising site

entries.sourceText: - **577. The Kruskal count** \[Gotcha\]: two people following card-count paths almost always land on the same card.
entries.title: A toy pair of paths can meet
entries.lens: the independent meeting-chance analogy to card-path coalescence

entries.sourceText: - **578. Cover time** \[Predict\]: how long until a random walker visits every node of a graph?
entries.title: Visit every node of a complete graph
entries.lens: the collection stages of a uniform complete-graph walk

entries.sourceText: - **579. Weather from umbrellas** \[Predict\]: infer hidden weather from whether a colleague carries an umbrella, with a hidden Markov model.
entries.title: An umbrella updates predicted weather
entries.lens: one measurement update using a supplied hidden-state prior

entries.sourceText: - **580. Machine up and down** \[Slider\]: a continuous-time chain of breakdowns and repairs; set rates and see availability.
entries.title: Repair and failure set availability
entries.lens: the rates of a two-state continuous-time machine

entries.sourceText: - **582. Step size** \[Slider\]: tiny steps crawl, huge steps get rejected; find the sweet spot by the acceptance meter.
entries.title: A large proposal can be rejected
entries.lens: the acceptance ratio under a symmetric standard-normal proposal

entries.sourceText: - **584. Burn-in** \[Predict\]: start far away and guess when the chain has forgotten its starting point.
entries.title: The starting state fades with steps
entries.lens: the finite-time transient in a specified chain

entries.sourceText: - **585. Four chains, one answer** \[Slider\]: start chains in different corners; R-hat drops toward 1 as they agree.
entries.title: Within and between chains disagree
entries.lens: the classic variance-ratio diagnostic under supplied summaries

entries.sourceText: - **586. The banana** \[Slider\]: random-walk Metropolis struggles along a curved posterior while Hamiltonian Monte Carlo glides through it.
entries.title: A curved target has a different energy
entries.lens: the energy cross-section of a stipulated banana density

entries.sourceText: - **587. Rolling marbles** \[Slider\]: HMC as a frictionless marble rolling across the negative log-density, with momentum.
entries.title: A momentum step follows a potential
entries.lens: the position and energy error of one harmonic leapfrog step

entries.sourceText: - **588. The U-turn** \[Slider\]: NUTS stops a trajectory once it starts doubling back; watch the tree grow and halt.
entries.title: A path begins moving back toward home
entries.lens: the one-dimensional U-turn dot-product check

entries.sourceText: - **589. Neal's funnel** \[Gotcha\]: a hierarchical posterior's narrow neck causes divergences; red dots mark where the sampler breaks.
entries.title: The funnel changes the coordinate scale
entries.lens: the scale transformation of a standardized latent coordinate

entries.sourceText: - **590. Gibbs zigzag** \[Slider\]: axis-aligned steps crawl along strongly correlated variables.
entries.title: Strong lag dependence wastes draws
entries.lens: a stipulated AR(1) approximation to correlated Gibbs output

entries.sourceText: - **591. The mode trap** \[Gotcha\]: a chain explores one peak of a two-peak distribution and never finds the other.
entries.title: A mode bottleneck keeps memory
entries.lens: a two-state analogy to slow inter-mode movement

entries.sourceText: - **592. Parallel tempering** \[Slider\]: hot chains roam freely and swap states with cold ones, crossing between modes.
entries.title: A temperature swap has a ratio
entries.lens: the two-energy tempering-swap probability

entries.sourceText: - **593. Effective sample size** \[Slider\]: 10,000 correlated draws may be worth only 300 independent ones.
entries.title: Many draws, little effective data
entries.lens: the mean-variance ESS of an explicit correlation model

entries.sourceText: - **594. Slice sampling** \[Slider\]: draw a horizontal slice under the curve and sample uniformly within it.
entries.title: A higher slice leaves a narrower set
entries.lens: the normal-density level set in a slice-sampling step

entries.sourceText: - **595. Particle swarm to posterior** \[Slider\]: sequential Monte Carlo moves a cloud of particles from prior to posterior in stages.
entries.title: Particles can have unequal mass
entries.lens: normalization and the importance-weight ESS

entries.sourceText: - **596. Find the dark matter** \[Predict\]: guess where invisible halos sit from distorted galaxy shapes, then watch an MCMC posterior cloud form, as in Kaggle's 2012 "Observing Dark Worlds".
entries.title: A one-axis halo-position posterior
entries.lens: a supplied normal-location likelihood rather than full lensing inference

entries.sourceText: - **597. Cracking a prison code** \[Story\]: MCMC over letter substitutions decoded a coded prisoner's message (Diaconis, 2009).
entries.title: A code proposal changes a supplied score
entries.lens: a symmetric-proposal acceptance ingredient rather than a live decoder

entries.sourceText: - **598. Denoising an image** \[Slider\]: Gibbs sampling with a "neighbors agree" prior cleans a noisy black-and-white picture.
entries.title: A pixel field competes with neighbors
entries.lens: the local binary-image conditional under a declared prior

entries.sourceText: - **599. A posterior of lines** \[Slider\]: draw 200 regression lines from the posterior; the band they form is the uncertainty.
entries.title: Uncertain slopes produce uncertain lines
entries.lens: the predictive variance from one uncertain linear weight

entries.sourceText: - **600. The thinning myth** \[Gotcha\]: discarding every other draw to cut autocorrelation usually throws away information.
entries.title: Thinning removes observations too
entries.lens: the exact finite AR(1) mean-variance comparison after every-other sampling

entries.sourceText: - **601. Fit the blob** \[Slider\]: drag a Gaussian's center and width over a strange posterior; an ELBO meter rewards the best fit.
entries.title: The evidence bound leaves a KL gap
entries.lens: the defining evidence-bound identity

entries.sourceText: - **604. Climbing the ELBO** \[Slider\]: watch the approximation slide and stretch as optimization runs.
entries.title: A smaller gap raises the bound
entries.lens: the stipulated approximation gap in an optimization objective

entries.sourceText: - **605. Laplace approximation** \[Slider\]: fit a parabola at the peak of the log-posterior; it works for round peaks, fails for skewed ones.
entries.title: Curvature gives a local Gaussian scale
entries.lens: the inverse-curvature approximation around one mode

entries.sourceText: - **606. Normalizing flows** \[Slider\]: a plain Gaussian is bent, step by step, into a spiral or a moon shape.
entries.title: One invertible step rescales a density
entries.lens: the Jacobian of a single affine flow component

entries.sourceText: - **607. Walk a VAE's latent space** \[Slider\]: drag a point across the latent plane and watch generated digits morph.
entries.title: A two-factor toy decoder
entries.lens: the constructed coordinate controls rather than generated digit images

entries.sourceText: - **608. The reparameterization trick** \[Slider\]: move the randomness outside the parameters so gradients can flow through samples.
entries.title: Keep the noise outside the parameters
entries.lens: the fixed-noise reparameterized sample and its derivatives

entries.sourceText: - **609. EP vs VI** \[Split\]: two approximate methods on the same posterior make different mistakes.
entries.title: A Gaussian approximation misses scale
entries.lens: the exact Gaussian-family KL rather than a full EP-versus-VI race

entries.sourceText: - **610. Inference by simulation** \[Slider\]: approximate Bayesian computation simulates data and keeps parameters whose output matches.
entries.title: A simulator summary passes a tolerance
entries.lens: the acceptance-distance ingredient of a toy ABC procedure

entries.sourceText: - **611. ABC tolerance** \[Slider\]: loosen the match tolerance and the posterior blurs toward the prior.
entries.title: A looser tolerance admits a candidate
entries.lens: the retained-summary predicate rather than a fitted ABC posterior

entries.sourceText: - **612. Repelling particles** \[Slider\]: Stein variational gradient descent pushes particles toward high density while they repel each other.
entries.title: Attraction and repulsion in one step
entries.lens: the two-particle SVGD field for a standard-normal target

entries.sourceText: - **613. Amortized inference** \[Slider\]: one trained network gives a posterior for any new dataset instantly.
entries.title: Evaluate a supplied inference mapping
entries.lens: the fixed mapping rather than an amortized network training run

entries.sourceText: - **614. Importance-weighted bounds** \[Slider\]: more samples per step tighten the bound toward the true evidence.
entries.title: Average weights before taking a log
entries.lens: the realized log-mean-exp statistic in an importance bound

entries.sourceText: - **615. Fast vs exact** \[Split\]: variational and Gibbs topic models race; one is faster, the other more accurate.
entries.title: Measure one toy approximation error
entries.lens: the Gaussian-family comparison rather than a measured inference race

entries.sourceText: - **616. Posterior collapse** \[Gotcha\]: a VAE's decoder learns to ignore its latent code entirely.
entries.title: An ignored code carries no information
entries.lens: the binary-channel analogy of latent-code collapse

entries.sourceText: - **617. Ensembles as posteriors** \[Slider\]: train several networks and treat their spread as an approximate posterior.
entries.title: Ensemble spread is an approximation
entries.lens: the supplied ensemble distribution rather than an exact posterior

entries.sourceText: - **618. Uncertain weights** \[Slider\]: a Bayesian neural network draws a different function for each weight sample.
entries.title: Weight uncertainty becomes output spread
entries.lens: the one-weight predictive uncertainty calculation

entries.sourceText: - **619. VI on a coin** \[Split\]: compare a variational answer with the exact beta posterior; they nearly match.
entries.title: An exact coin posterior as a benchmark
entries.lens: the exact conjugate mean before assessing an approximation

entries.sourceText: - **620. Neural posterior estimation** \[Slider\]: train on simulations, then read off a posterior for an epidemic model's parameters.
entries.title: A supplied simulation likelihood ratio
entries.lens: the numerical posterior update rather than a trained neural estimator

entries.sourceText: - **621. Radon by county** \[Slider\]: county estimates of home radon levels slide between their own data and the state average (Gelman & Hill, 2007).
entries.title: A small county borrows more strength
entries.lens: the fixed-hyperparameter normal pooling weight

entries.sourceText: - **623. Shrinkage arrows** \[Slider\]: arrows show each group's raw estimate moving toward the mean, longest for the smallest groups.
entries.title: Information controls group shrinkage
entries.lens: the group-size dependence of a stated shrinkage update

entries.sourceText: - **624. Eight schools** \[Story\]: coaching effects in eight schools, a classic test case for hierarchical models (Rubin, 1981).
entries.title: One school under a population prior
entries.lens: a single-group normal update rather than a fitted eight-school model

entries.sourceText: - **625. Star ratings, shrunk** \[Slider\]: products with 3 reviews get pulled toward their category average; those with 3,000 barely move.
entries.title: Three reviews versus three thousand
entries.lens: the data weight in a normal ratings-pooling illustration

entries.sourceText: - **626. Batting averages** \[Slider\]: a hierarchical model predicts end-of-season averages from April data better than raw averages.
entries.title: Early batting averages get pooled
entries.lens: the evidence size under a fixed normal approximation

entries.sourceText: - **628. Group-level predictors** \[Slider\]: county uranium levels explain some of the variation in county radon averages.
entries.title: A group predictor changes the prior mean
entries.lens: the supplied group-level prior prediction

entries.sourceText: - **629. New sellers** \[Slider\]: a marketplace scores a seller with 2 orders by borrowing strength from similar sellers.
entries.title: A new seller has little direct evidence
entries.lens: the prior-data weighting for an explicit seller model

entries.sourceText: - **630. MRP map** \[Slider\]: a skewed national survey is modeled and reweighted into credible state-by-state estimates.
entries.title: Poststratify supplied group predictions
entries.lens: target-population weights rather than a complete fitted MRP model

entries.sourceText: - **631. Fixing the funnel** \[Split\]: the same model in centered and non-centered form; one samples cleanly.
entries.title: The same standardized latent coordinate
entries.lens: the nonlinear scale mapping in a noncentered parameterization

entries.sourceText: - **632. Group variance prior** \[Slider\]: change the prior on between-group spread and watch pooling strength change.
entries.title: Between-group variance controls pooling
entries.lens: the fixed group-variance input in a hierarchical update

entries.sourceText: - **633. Small-area estimates** \[Slider\]: estimate unemployment in tiny districts by pooling with similar ones.
entries.title: A tiny district gets more pooling
entries.lens: the sample information behind a small-area estimate

entries.sourceText: - **634. Hospital league tables** \[Slider\]: a funnel plot shows most "worst" hospitals are just small ones with noisy rates.
entries.title: Small hospitals have noisier proportions
entries.lens: the binomial sampling-spread facet of a funnel plot

entries.sourceText: - **635. Teacher value-added** \[Slider\]: shrinking estimates for teachers with few students tames wild rankings.
entries.title: Few students leave a noisy teacher score
entries.lens: the information weight under a stipulated teacher-effect prior

entries.sourceText: - **636. A/B tests in 30 countries** \[Slider\]: pool country-level results so tiny markets don't produce crazy effects.
entries.title: Tiny markets borrow from a common mean
entries.lens: the normal pooling weight across toy market estimates

entries.sourceText: - **637. Random-effects meta-analysis** \[Slider\]: combine studies whose true effects vary; the forest plot updates live.
entries.title: Between-study spread changes the weights
entries.lens: the assumed heterogeneity in a two-study meta-analysis

entries.sourceText: - **638. Students and questions** \[Slider\]: item response theory estimates each student's ability and each question's difficulty together.
entries.title: Ability minus difficulty sets the odds
entries.lens: the one-parameter logistic item-response rule

entries.sourceText: - **639. Personal baselines** \[Slider\]: repeated measurements per person; a per-person intercept separates people from time.
entries.title: A personal baseline shifts a time trend
entries.lens: the intercept term separate from a stipulated time slope

entries.sourceText: - **640. Thousands of ads** \[Slider\]: estimate click-through for many ads with few impressions each by pooling within campaign.
entries.title: Rare ad clicks meet prior counts
entries.lens: the conjugate predictive mean for a supplied campaign prior

entries.sourceText: - **641. Tap to add data** \[Slider\]: tap the screen to drop points; the GP mean bends through them and the uncertainty band pinches at each one.
entries.title: One data point bends a GP mean
entries.lens: the one-observation Gaussian conditional update

entries.sourceText: - **643. Kernel zoo** \[Split\]: the same points under RBF, Matérn, periodic and linear kernels.
entries.title: Two kernels assign different similarity
entries.lens: the declared covariance function at one distance

entries.sourceText: - **644. Mauna Loa CO₂** \[Slider\]: add a trend kernel, a yearly periodic kernel and noise to fit the famous curve and forecast it.
entries.title: A periodic component recognizes a cycle
entries.lens: the periodic covariance ingredient rather than a full CO2 fit

entries.sourceText: - **645. Functions from the prior** \[Slider\]: draw random functions from a GP before seeing any data.
entries.title: A prior linear-function variance
entries.lens: the Gaussian linear-function prior as a simple process example

entries.sourceText: - **646. Noise level** \[Slider\]: raise assumed noise and the curve stops passing exactly through each point.
entries.title: More observation noise softens the fit
entries.lens: the noise term of a one-point GP update

entries.sourceText: - **648. Let the data choose** \[Slider\]: the marginal likelihood surface over length scale and noise has a clear peak.
entries.title: A marginal density trades fit and spread
entries.lens: the one-observation marginal-likelihood ingredient

entries.sourceText: - **649. You vs the optimizer** \[Measure\]: find the peak of a hidden function in 10 tries, then watch Bayesian optimization do it.
entries.title: Uncertainty offers expected improvement
entries.lens: the normal predictive improvement at two candidate points

entries.sourceText: - **650. Acquisition functions** \[Split\]: expected improvement, upper confidence bound and probability of improvement pick different next points.
entries.title: Expected improvement at one point
entries.lens: one acquisition function rather than a full optimizer comparison

entries.sourceText: - **651. Explore or exploit** \[Slider\]: raise UCB's exploration weight and the optimizer spends more tries in uncertain regions.
entries.title: An exploration weight changes the score
entries.lens: the uncertainty bonus in a declared acquisition rule

entries.sourceText: - **652. Optimized cookies** \[Story\]: Google used Bayesian optimization to tune a chocolate chip cookie recipe through tasting rounds (Kochanski et al., 2017).
entries.title: A tasting-score acquisition value
entries.lens: the expected-improvement ingredient of a recipe-search analogy

entries.sourceText: - **653. GP classification** \[Slider\]: a smooth probability surface separates two classes, uncertain where they mix.
entries.title: Latent uncertainty softens a class score
entries.lens: the displayed logistic-normal approximation

entries.sourceText: - **654. Kriging a terrain** \[Slider\]: interpolate a 2D elevation map from scattered surveys, a method born in mining.
entries.title: One elevation point informs nearby land
entries.lens: the isotropic one-observation kriging ingredient

entries.sourceText: - **655. Inducing points** \[Slider\]: summarize 10,000 points with 20 inducing points and see what's lost.
entries.title: Inducing points change a work proxy
entries.lens: the stated dense-versus-approximate operation counts

entries.sourceText: - **656. GP vs neural net** \[Split\]: away from data, the GP admits it doesn't know; the network extrapolates confidently.
entries.title: Away from data, GP variance grows
entries.lens: the GP component rather than a trained neural-net comparison

entries.sourceText: - **657. Changepoints** \[Slider\]: a GP whose kernel switches at a changepoint captures a sudden regime shift.
entries.title: A changed slope alters extrapolation
entries.lens: the piecewise mean component of a changepoint model

entries.sourceText: - **658. Infinitely wide networks** \[Gotcha\]: as a neural net's layers grow infinitely wide, it becomes a Gaussian process.
entries.title: Scale variances while adding units
entries.lens: the finite variance-scaling ingredient of a wide-network limit

entries.sourceText: - **659. Several outputs at once** \[Slider\]: a multi-output GP lets sparse data in one series borrow from another.
entries.title: One output informs a correlated output
entries.lens: the cross-covariance in a two-output Gaussian update

entries.sourceText: - **660. Where to measure next** \[Slider\]: active learning places the next sensor where the GP is most uncertain.
entries.title: Measure where variance is high
entries.lens: the conditional variance used in a toy active-learning decision

entries.sourceText: - **661. Noisy GPS** \[Slider\]: a car's true path, scattered GPS fixes, and a Kalman estimate that stays smooth and close.
entries.title: A noisy position measurement gets a gain
entries.lens: the scalar linear-Gaussian predict-update calculation

entries.sourceText: - **663. Predict, then update** \[Slider\]: an uncertainty ellipse grows with each prediction and shrinks with each measurement.
entries.title: Prediction and measurement change spread
entries.lens: the process-variance input in a scalar filtering step

entries.sourceText: - **664. Sensor fusion** \[Slider\]: combine jumpy GPS with drifting motion sensors; together they beat either alone.
entries.title: Fuse two independent scalar sensors
entries.lens: the relative precisions of two stated sensor measurements

entries.sourceText: - **666. Lost robot** \[Slider\]: a particle filter scatters guesses through a maze; they collapse onto the robot's true location.
entries.title: Robot-location particles get weights
entries.lens: the weight normalization ingredient of particle localization

entries.sourceText: - **667. Particle collapse** \[Slider\]: without resampling, almost all weight lands on one particle.
entries.title: One particle can dominate the weight
entries.lens: the importance-weight ESS before any resampling step

entries.sourceText: - **668. Curved motion** \[Split\]: extended and unscented Kalman filters track a turning target with different errors.
entries.title: Curvature changes a predicted mean
entries.lens: the exact transformed moment versus a mean linearization
